scope: Full audit of the acme-console repository on branch main (commit a1b2c3d): 47 route handlers, 12 frontend components carrying role gates, 6 deploy files, and the git history since repository creation.
methodology: The five categories were mapped onto the detected stack as follows: (1) tenant isolation is a manual organization_id predicate in the Drizzle repository layer, there is no RLS in Postgres; (2) each React role gate was cross-referenced one by one against its Hono handler; (3) IDOR was checked across all 47 handlers including those keyed by UUID; (4) the secret sweep covered source, docker-compose, GitHub Actions workflows, the Vite bundle, and git history via git log -p -S; (5) XSS covered innerHTML and dangerouslySetInnerHTML sinks on the frontend and email templates on the backend.
stack: JWT signed with HS256, verified in middleware
React 18 + Vite, no sanitization library installed

findings.title: Report export endpoint does not filter by organization
findings.why: The handler requires authentication but never scopes the result set to the caller's organization. Any authenticated user, from any tenant, calls GET /reports/export?from=2020-01-01&to=2030-01-01 and receives a CSV of every invoice on the platform.
findings.preconditions: None. A valid account from the public /signup flow is enough.
findings.impact: Complete cross-tenant disclosure of financial data: amounts, customer names, and dates for every organization.
findings.fix: Add the organization predicate the rest of the repository already uses: and(eq(invoices.organizationId, c.get('session').organizationId), ...). Consider promoting this to RLS in Postgres so a handler cannot forget it.

findings.title: JWT signing secret has a public default and no startup validation
findings.why: The default value sits in a public repository. A deploy that forgets to set JWT_SECRET comes up silently on a known secret, and nothing at boot refuses. With it, an attacker signs an arbitrary token with any sub and organizationId and becomes admin of any tenant.
findings.preconditions: The environment must not define JWT_SECRET. Nothing in the code signals that this happened.
findings.impact: Full identity forgery, including escalation to admin of any organization.
findings.fix: Remove the default in both places and add a boot check that throws when JWT_SECRET is absent or matches any known value. Rotate the production secret, since the value has been exposed.

findings.title: Document DELETE trusts the route ID without an ownership check
findings.why: The handler deletes by raw id. No clause ties the document to the session's organization. A UUID belonging to another tenant, obtained from a share link or an export, is enough to destroy the record.
findings.preconditions: The attacker needs the UUID. F1 supplies exactly that.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant data destruction with no authorization trail.
findings.fix: Use the requireDocAccess() helper the read handlers already apply, or include eq(documents.organizationId, session.organizationId) in the where clause.

findings.title: Member invite route performs no server-side role check
findings.why: The invite button is hidden from non-admins, but requireAuth only proves authentication. An ordinary member POSTs to /members/invite directly and invites any address, including with role 'admin', escalating their own access through a second signup.
findings.preconditions: Being an ordinary member of any organization.
findings.impact: Horizontal and vertical privilege escalation inside the tenant.
findings.fix: Apply the existing requireRole('admin') middleware from src/middleware/rbac.ts:22, and validate the role field against an allowlist.

findings.title: Project name rendered through dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.why: displayName comes from the project creation form with no sanitization at either end. A member stores as the name and the script runs in the browser of every other member who opens the project, admins included.
findings.preconditions: None beyond being able to create or rename a project.
findings.impact: Stored XSS reaching admin sessions within the tenant.
findings.fix: Render as plain text. If HTML is intentional, install DOMPurify (absent from package.json) and sanitize before rendering.

findings.title: Development database credential inlined in compose
findings.why: Fixed credential for a local Postgres that is not exposed outside the compose network. Reachable only by someone who already has the developer's machine.
findings.preconditions: Local access to a development machine.
findings.impact: Low. No production data lives in this database.
findings.fix: Move to an untracked local .env file, more for hygiene than for risk.

findings.title: Supabase anon key present in the frontend bundle
findings.why: The anon key is public by design and the VITE_ prefix makes that explicit. Recorded only to confirm the bundle sweep ran and that no service-role key was found.
findings.impact: None, provided server-side access policies are correct.
findings.fix: No action. Confirmed the service-role key appears in no file reachable by the build.

strengths.title: Object-level authorization across document read handlers
strengths.evidence: src/routes/documents.ts - all 9 GET handlers load through requireDocAccess() (:14), which joins on organization_id taken from the session. Verified line by line: :31, :48, :66, :83, :97, :112, :130, :158, :171. Only the DELETE (:142, finding F3) escapes the helper.

strengths.title: Parameterized queries across all data access
strengths.evidence: No string concatenation into SQL at any of the 63 data-access sites. Every access goes through Drizzle, which parameterizes. Searched for sql.raw and interpolated template literals: zero occurrences outside migrations.

strengths.title: JWT verification with a pinned algorithm
strengths.evidence: src/middleware/auth.ts:19 - jwtVerify with an explicit algorithms: ['HS256'], exp and iss validated (:24-27). Does not accept alg none or algorithm substitution. The problem in F2 is the secret, not the verification.

strengths.title: Git history clean of live secrets
strengths.evidence: git log -p -S across 14 key patterns (sk-, ghp_, AKIA, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, among others) over 1,204 commits: no hits. No .env was ever tracked, confirmed via git log --all --name-only -- '*.env'.

weaknesses: Tenant isolation rests on a manual predicate repeated in 63 places. It is correct in 62 of them, and the single omission (F1) exposes the entire financial dataset. The mechanism has no safety net.
Role authorization lives only on the frontend for at least one sensitive route (F4), and the RBAC middleware exists but is applied inconsistently.
Secrets carry public defaults and nothing at boot refuses to start on them (F2), which turns a forgotten deploy variable into full compromise.

not_applicable.reason: This project's Postgres does not use RLS. The audited equivalent was the manual organization_id predicate in the Drizzle repository layer, covered under category 1.
Outside the five requested categories, but checked incidentally during the data-access sweep and recorded as a strength.

coverage.checked: 63 data-access sites, 21 of them returning collections
12 frontend role gates cross-referenced against 12 endpoints
source, 6 deploy files, Vite bundle, 1,204 commits

recommendations.text: Rotate JWT_SECRET in production and add boot validation that refuses known defaults.
Fix the report export and the document DELETE, the two paths that leak or destroy cross-tenant data today.
Apply requireRole('admin') across all member-management routes and audit the rest of the router against the frontend gates.
Adopt RLS in Postgres for organization_id, so that forgetting the predicate stops being sufficient to leak data.
Install DOMPurify and sanitize the HTML sinks, or drop the use of dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
Move development credentials out of compose into an untracked local .env.

# [Security] Report export leaks invoices across all tenants

**Labels:** `security`, `severity:critical`

## Problem

The `GET /reports/export` handler requires authentication but does not scope the result set to the caller's organization. Any authenticated user retrieves invoices for the entire platform.

## Evidence

`src/routes/reports.ts:88-104`

```ts
app.get('/reports/export', requireAuth, async (c) => {
  const rows = await db.select().from(invoices)
    .where(between(invoices.issuedAt, from, to));
  return c.body(toCsv(rows), 200, { 'content-type': 'text/csv' });
});
```

## Impact

Cross-tenant disclosure of financial data. No precondition: a account from the public signup flow is enough.

## Suggested fix

Include the organization predicate already used elsewhere in the repository:

```ts
.where(and(
  eq(invoices.organizationId, c.get('session').organizationId),
  between(invoices.issuedAt, from, to),
))
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The handler filters by `organizationId` taken from the session, never from the request
- [ ] An integration test with two tenants confirms A cannot see B's invoices
- [ ] A sweep of the other 20 collection endpoints confirms the same predicate
- [ ] Export access logging records organization and user

# [Security] Public secret defaults and missing startup validation

**Labels:** `security`, `severity:critical`

## Problem

Two places define a default value for secrets committed to the repository, and nothing at boot refuses to start on them. A deploy that forgets the variable comes up on a publicly known secret.

## Evidence

`docker-compose.yml:23`

```yaml
JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-dev-secret-change-me}
```

`src/env.ts:11`

```ts
export const env = { jwtSecret: process.env.JWT_SECRET ?? 'dev-secret-change-me' };
```

## Impact

With the secret known, an attacker signs a token carrying any `sub` and `organizationId`, becoming admin of any tenant.

## Suggested fix

Remove the defaults and fail at boot:

```ts
const FORBIDDEN = new Set(['dev-secret-change-me', 'changeme', 'secret']);
if (!process.env.JWT_SECRET || FORBIDDEN.has(process.env.JWT_SECRET)) {
  throw new Error('JWT_SECRET missing or set to a default value');
}
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No secret default remains in compose or in source
- [ ] The process fails at boot without `JWT_SECRET` or with a denylisted value
- [ ] `JWT_SECRET` rotated in production
- [ ] Tests cover boot with the variable absent and with a default value
